stories.headline: Juniper Ridge drops three first sets and wins 6-1 at Liberty Hill
stories.byline: By Dale Kreuger | Courier staff writer
body: Ezekiel Amoore walked to the fence at Liberty Hill Monday down a set, 6-1 to junior Jaxton Martin, and coach Ray Okafor let him stand there without a word. Amoore won the next two sets 7-5, 6-3. Later in the afternoon two of his teammates came back from a lost first set of their own, and the defending 5A champions won their opener 6-1.
Amoore was the senior Okafor settled on at first singles after a week of shuffling.
"Zeke was tight for a set and then he wasn't," Okafor said. "I'd rather he gets that out of his system in Liberty Hill than in October."

Levi Chesnut, the sophomore who went 16-0 as a freshman, lost the first set 6-3 to Ethan Cross at No. 4 singles and then won 12 of the last 14 games. Senior Jonah Smith followed the same route at No. 5, 4-6, 6-0, 6-4. Deon Rennick (6-3, 7-6) and Joshua Butcher (6-3, 6-1) won in straight sets at second and third singles.

Liberty Hill's point came at No. 1 doubles, where seniors Brooks Marco and Kannon Benito beat Gabriel Clark and Avery Hermes 7-6, 2-6, 6-4. "Two seniors who've played together since middle school," Liberty Hill coach Gary Tomczak said. "That's the one I'll remember from tonight."
Juniper Ridge (1-0) is home Tuesday against Pacersburg and Wednesday against Westfield Friends.

stories.headline: Dukes wins 6-1, 6-1 in his first match at the top for Altamonte
stories.byline: By Dale Kreuger | Courier staff writer
body: The first match to finish at Senator Gray on the opening day was the one Altamonte coach Paul Ostrowski had changed over the summer. Roman Dukes, a senior who played doubles nearly all of last season, beat Cranston Diggins at first singles, and Altamonte swept the crosstown opener 7-0.
Grant Labbé, who held that spot a year ago and went 8-23, moved down one place and beat John Jensen 6-2, 6-4.
"Grant came to me in June and said he wanted Roman to have a shot at one," Ostrowski said. "You don't get that from many seniors."

Dorian Sadiq, Liam Mochizuki and Michael Crawford won the last three singles positions without dropping a set. Two freshmen, Reed Fong and Carter Fiore, won 6-4, 6-2 at No. 1 doubles, and Joe Curran and sophomore Michael Williams came back from a first-set tiebreak at No. 2 to win 6-7, 6-2, 6-4.
Altamonte opens the Big Basin League Saturday at Anse Doree. Senator Gray plays at Bitterroot Wednesday and at Ditch Fork Thursday.

stories.headline: Six of the first 12 go 4-3
body: Calder. A team that won eight duals a year ago beat Central West End, a 5A Octofinalist, 5-2 at home. The point that held the dual together came from a freshman and a sophomore. Kostas Maniatis and Leroy Ryang beat seniors Isaiah Conway and Lucas Pogba 7-6, 7-5 at No. 1 doubles, and the two were still sitting on the fence by the court an hour later, watching the last singles match finish. Junior Charles Williams beat Nico Buchner 6-1, 7-6 at the top of the order.

Marlow County. Won 4-3 at Carolina Island with two freshmen in the winning column: Muhammad King at No. 5 singles (6-3, 7-5) and Abram Conn, who partnered senior Denis Strelkov to a 6-3, 6-3 win at No. 1 doubles. Sophomore Troy Holmes lost his first set 6-1 at third singles and won 6-1, 6-2.
Aspen Hollow. Also 4-3, at Seamus Town, with freshman Andre Salaun winning 6-4, 7-6 at fifth singles.
The rest of the 4-3s. Copper Gap over Cornerstone Christian, Telfair Country Day at Doyle Pass, Trout Lake at Star Hollow and Fountain Park at Meridian Regional.
Silton Ridge. The Desert Sky League champion lost all seven matches at Espoo.
California Canyons. Hudson Chiu lost a first-set tiebreak to Rohan Lancaster and won 6-2, 6-1 in a 5-2 win at Summervale.

stories.headline: League play starts Tuesday
body: Marlow County opens the Dual County League at home Tuesday against Archbishop Quinlan. Wednesday's league duals send Calder home against Obama, Trout Lake home against Cornerstone Christian, Central West End to Frontier and California Canyons to Pomar.
Thursday brings Copper Gap against Aspen Hollow in the Desert Sky League, Juniper Ridge at Cedar Exchange and Liberty Hill at Tidewater Catholic.
